system.longDesc:
Capacity: 0 Slots

Augmentations make it easy to install some type of “kill-switch” able to render the subject dead instantly, from a tiny explosive at the base of the brainstem to a time- or signal-release toxin, an electrical jolt that stops the heart, or an artificial stroke from blood vessel constriction. In some cases, a kill-switch might also be able to merely render you unconscious or incapacitate you with overwhelming pain instead of killing you. Usually, a kill-switch can be activated remotely, although it might also be on a timer, or keyed to some other conditions, such as a GPS sensor for when you leave or enter a particular place, or if you are exposed to a particular trigger. In cyberpunk fiction, these types of self-destruct implants are often used as “insurance policies” to protect investments and prevent augments from simply taking off with a lot of expensive hardware in them.

Modern AGE Game Masters can use kill-switch implants as a kind of Complication for characters who exceed their Capacity (see Complications at the start of this chapter). In essence, rather than imposing a particular stunt-effect, the Complication is that the character is beholden to whomever holds the control for their kill-switch. This provides the story explanation for why the character has augmentations in excess of their normal Capacity, and how they are “paying”

for them. Generally, a kill-switch should be considered worth at least a 4-point Complication, given how it restricts the character’s options. Technically, it is a 6-point Complication in its effect, but its value is reduced because its effect is known and meant not to be used unless necessary.
